scenes.heading: Introducing polynomials
scenes.sub: The language of x³, x² and friends
scenes.say: Roller-coaster tracks, profit models and the volume of a box can all be written as polynomials. Let's learn how to read them and work with them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A train: the engine at the front leads the way
scenes.science: The leading term (highest power) controls the polynomial
scenes.breaks: A polynomial can skip powers, like x³ + 1 with no x² term, but a train can't skip a carriage.
scenes.say: Think of a polynomial as a train. Each term is a carriage, lined up from the highest power to the lowest. The engine at the front, the leading term, decides where the train is heading.

scenes.heading: Naming the parts
scenes.say: Take P of x equals five x cubed minus two x squared plus x minus eight. The degree is the highest power, three. The leading coefficient is five. The constant term is negative eight. And remember: only whole-number powers are allowed.
scenes.caption: Take P(x) = 5x³ − 2x² + x − 8. The degree is the highest power, 3. The leading coefficient is 5. The constant term is −8. Only whole-number powers are allowed.

scenes.heading: Using P(x) notation
scenes.question: P(x) = 2x³ − 3x² + x − 5. Find P(2).
scenes.say: P of two means replace every x with two. Two times eight, minus three times four, plus two, minus five. That's sixteen minus twelve plus two minus five, which is one.
scenes.caption: P(2) means replace every x with 2: 2(8) − 3(4) + 2 − 5 = 16 − 12 + 2 − 5 = 1.

scenes.heading: Multiplying polynomials
scenes.question: Expand (x + 2)(x² − 3x + 4).
scenes.say: To multiply, every term meets every term. x times the trinomial gives x cubed minus three x squared plus four x. Two times it gives two x squared minus six x plus eight. Collect like terms: x cubed minus x squared minus two x plus eight.
scenes.caption: Every term meets every term. x × the trinomial: x³ − 3x² + 4x. 2 × it: 2x² − 6x + 8. Collect: x³ − x² − 2x + 8.

scenes.heading: The leading coefficient sets the shape
notes: y = x³ rises to the right
scenes.say: First the axes, then the curves. y equals x cubed rises from bottom left to top right. Make the leading coefficient negative and the graph flips: y equals negative x cubed falls to the right.
scenes.caption: y = x³ rises from bottom left to top right. With a negative leading coefficient the graph flips: y = −x³ falls to the right.

scenes.heading: A cubic crosses the x-axis up to 3 times
scenes.say: Here is y equals x cubed minus two x squared minus five x plus six. Watch it cross the x-axis at negative two, one and three. It cuts the y-axis at six, the constant term, because P of zero is always the constant.
scenes.caption: y = x³ − 2x² − 5x + 6 crosses the x-axis at −2, 1 and 3, and the y-axis at 6, the constant term, because P(0) is always the constant.

points: Multiply every term by every term
Degree n: at most n x-intercepts
scenes.say: Quick recap. The degree is the highest power. P of a means substitute. When multiplying, every term meets every term, and the degrees add. Now try the practice questions!
